# Streaming & AI Unlock Check (流媒体/AI 解锁检测)

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Which streaming and AI services work on your IP, and which country does each one see? [Streaming & AI Unlock Check](https://unlock.1ms.dog) asks 150 services from your browser — Netflix, Disney+, TikTok, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and more — over the route your proxy picks for each one, and says how sure each verdict is.

**Live:** https://unlock.1ms.dog

## Why a web page

The well-known unlock scripts (RegionRestrictionCheck and its forks) run `curl` on a server, so they test that server's IP. People with rule-based proxies (Clash, Surge, Shadowrocket, sing-box) route each site differently; only a check from their own browser takes the same route their Netflix or ChatGPT tab takes. A browser can't read most sites' answers (no CORS), so each check uses the strongest signal a static page can get, and labels it:

| Label | How | Services |
|---|---|---|
| **Official API** | The service's own region API, readable from any page (CORS). The same endpoint the command-line scripts read. | ChatGPT (`api.openai.com/compliance/cookie_requirements` + its trace), DAZN, Philo, NBC, Shudder, beIN CONNECT, KKTV, TVB Anywhere+, SBS On Demand, FOD, DMM TV, ZDF, NHK ONE, TELASA, 10 Play, ITVX, Molotov, Sling TV, A&E, Mango TV |
| **Official API (script)** | An answer only given as a script (JSONP): run in `/assets/jsonp.html`, a sandboxed frame with no origin of its own whose policy only lets those services’ scripts run, and posted back. | BBC iPlayer (media selector: `geolocation` outside the UK), Tencent Video (`getinfo`: `em` 0 plays) |
| **Its location** | Cloudflare's `/cdn-cgi/trace` on the service's own domain (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) gives the country that edge sees, checked against the service's published list. | Claude, Copilot, Grok, Perplexity, Le Chat, Poe, Character.AI, Crunchyroll, X, J:COM STREAM, 4GTV, LiTV, Bahamut Anime Crazy, NLZIET, The CW, DIRECTV Stream |
| **Redirect test** | Redirect counting, below. | Netflix (region), Disney+, Peacock, Pandora, Tubi (a redirect from the front page outside their regions only), Paramount+, Viu (their own “not available here” page stays put outside their regions and sends everyone else home) |
| **Guess** | Nothing of the service's own is readable: it is reachable over your route, and the country most services see is checked against its published list. | Gemini, Meta AI, Twitch, Prime Video, Apple TV+, HBO Max, Hulu, Pluto TV, ESPN+, Fubo, Viki, Bilibili TV, Spotify, Deezer, SoundCloud, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Reddit, Facebook, Messenger, Threads, Signal, LINE, Snapchat, Pinterest, Google, Wikipedia, Roblox, ABEMA, U-NEXT, TVer, Hulu Japan, Lemino, d Anime Store, WOWOW, radiko, VideoMarket, Rakuten TV Japan, mora, Wavve, TVING, Coupang Play, Watcha, SPOTV NOW, Hami Video, myVideo, friDay Video, ofiii, LINE TV, myTV SUPER, Now E, ViuTV, HOY TV, JioHotstar, Sony LIV, Tata Play Binge, MX Player, meWATCH, StarHub TV+, Vidio, Mola, TrueID, AIS PLAY, sooka, Galaxy Play, TV360, K+, Stan, Binge, Kayo Sports, 7plus, ABC iview, 9Now, Optus Sport, ThreeNow, Neon, Sky Go NZ, Channel 4, My5, Sky Go, france.tv, Joyn, RTL+, Sky Go Germany, Sky Switzerland, RaiPlay, Movistar Plus+, NPO Start, Videoland, Amediateka, STARZ, MGM+, FX, NFL+, TLC GO, CBC Gem, Crave, Bilibili, iQIYI, Youku, NetEase Cloud Music |

Country lists come from the services: [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/supported-countries), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/supported-countries), [Gemini app](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13575153) (it includes Hong Kong and Macau; the Gemini API list doesn't), [Netflix](https://help.netflix.com/en/node/14164).

### Redirect counting

A browser follows at most 20 redirects (Chrome, Firefox; Safari fewer) and then fails the request. `public/_redirects` makes `/h/<n>/<host>/<path>` redirect n times on this site, the last time to `https://<host>/<path>`. Sending a `no-cors` request through `MAX − k` of ours loads only when the service adds at most `k` of its own, so the page counts the service's redirects without reading anything. The limit is measured first (`/hop.txt`), so other browsers work too. The rules are static: the asset server answers them without running a script (free, unmetered).

Measured in Chrome 141 on 2026-11-01 (a Japanese exit; the US numbers from a server in Los Angeles):

| Request | Japan | US |
|---|---|---|
| `netflix.com/jp/` | 0 redirects | 2 |
| `netflix.com/us/`, `/sg/`, `/de/`, `/gb/`… | 2 | `/us/` → `/`: 1 |
| `netflix.com/` | 1 (→ `/jp-en/`) | 0 |
| `peacocktv.com/` | 1 (→ `/unavailable`) | 0 |
| `disneyplus.com/` | 0 | 0 |

So Netflix answers only its own country's path directly: trying the countries other services see first finds the Netflix region in one or two requests. On Cloudflare (unlock.1ms.dog, 2026-11-01) the static rules redirect as above, the last hop leaving the site, and a live run counts the same. Netflix serves crawlers without redirects, so test with a normal browser user agent (headless Chrome's `HeadlessChrome` gets 0 everywhere).

### What a browser can't tell

- **Netflix catalog:** a region is found, but whether licensed (non-Netflix) titles play isn't visible; Netflix limits many proxy and datacenter IPs to its own shows. The scripts read this from the title page's body, which a browser can't.
- **Gemini:** Google locates IPs with its own database (the "sent to China" problem), and no Google endpoint a page can read reveals it. Gemini is marked inferred.
- **New redirect tests** (2026-11-04): Pandora, Tubi and Paramount+ measured from Japan and the US, Viu from Japan, Hong Kong and the US. Pluto TV, ESPN+ and Fubo redirect inside their regions too (ESPN+ to `/denied` from a US proxy), so they are inferred.
- **Not included on purpose:** Sora (the app closed in 2026), PlayStation Store (not region-locked: nothing to tell), Midjourney (its pages refuse other sites). Checks that need a third party's embedded API keys or that submit sign-up forms (Spotify, Catchplay, Tving and others in the scripts). YouTube Premium: no readable signal yet.

Pages whose resource policy refuses other sites (`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`/`same-site`: claude.ai/login, gemini.google.com, aistudio.google.com) can't be counted either: the browser fails them whatever the status.

### Other findings

- Services see different countries when rules split traffic: in testing, SBS On Demand saw Hong Kong while 15 others saw Japan. The page lists which services see which country, and links to EgressLens on 1ms.dog.
- Browser time zone vs. the services' country: AI services use it as a proxy signal.

**Private by design:** static files only. Your browser talks to each service directly; no result is sent to the site. Share links carry each service's verdict and country, never an IP.

### After a run

- **Report card:** a grade per category (S at 95% of the services with an answer, then A 80%, B 60%, C 40%, D), and the places whose own regional services work. The main grades go on the share card too.
- **Route advice:** for a service that isn't available over the route it took, another of your exits where it is (send its domain there), or none (it needs a node elsewhere); for one that doesn't open, its domain to check in your rules.
- **IP identity:** whether Wikipedia blocks the address from editing as an open proxy or hosting range (its API answers any site, with the host it names), and whether Sling TV refused it as a proxy.
- **Since your last run** and **your collection** (Netflix regions, exit countries, regional TV places seen): kept in this browser only (`localStorage`, the last 10 runs, verdicts and countries, no address).

Every check in the command-line scripts, and why each is or isn't here: [docs/coverage.md](docs/coverage.md).

## Pages

Every language (`/`, `/zh-cn/`, `/zh-tw/`, `/ja/`, `/ko/`, `/es/`, `/fr/`, `/de/`, `/pt/`, `/ru/`) has the main page, a page per category (`/ai/`, `/streaming/`, `/social/`, `/regional/`) and a page per service (`/netflix/`, `/chatgpt/`, `/claude/`…), each with its own title, questions and preview image; a service's page leads with its verdict and lists where it is offered.

## Self-hosting

`public/` is committed, so nothing needs building unless you change the code.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yt1988/unlock-check
cd unlock-check
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy        # a static-assets Worker: no script, free and unmetered
```

`wrangler.toml` turns off `*.workers.dev` and preview URLs; bind your own domain under **Workers & Pages → unlock → Settings → Domains & Routes**, or set `workers_dev = true` for a quick test. Another static host works if it supports Cloudflare-style `_headers` and `_redirects` (Cloudflare Pages, Netlify); without `_redirects`, Netflix, Disney+ and Peacock show as reachable only.

To put your own domain into canonical links and the sitemap:

```bash
npm install
SITE_URL=https://unlock.example.com npm run build
```

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:8787, with the production headers and the redirect chain
CHECK=http://127.0.0.1:8787 npm run dev   # also the checkup embed mode: open http://127.0.0.1:8787/__checkup.html
npm run build      # regenerate public/ after changing src/ (commit public/)
npm test           # public/ up to date, page contract, SEO, and the logic tests
npm run icons      # download the services' icons into public/assets/svc/ after adding a service (commit them)
npm run og         # redraw the link-preview images in public/og/ after changing a headline (commit them)
```

```
src/services.mjs     the services: category, probe, published country list
src/lib.mjs          pure logic (answer readers, verdicts, share links), unit-tested
src/app.js           browser code: asks the services, counts redirects, renders, shares
src/i18n/*.mjs       strings for 10 languages
scripts/build.mjs    builds public/: every page, _redirects, _headers, sitemap
```

Adding a service: an entry in `src/services.mjs` (a reader in `src/lib.mjs` for an API), its slug, then `npm run build && npm run og`.
